key_insight: The paper introduces AGL1K, the first large-scale audio geo-localization benchmark for audio-language models spanning 72 countries, revealing that current ALMs struggle to infer geographic origin from audio and that high-quality audio–location pairs are essential for progress.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of reliable, diverse audio–location data and a standardized benchmark for evaluating audio-language models on geo-localization tasks.
method: Curate AGL1K: assemble and validate high-quality audio–location pairs covering 72 countries and territories.
Design a benchmark suite and evaluation protocol tailored to audio-language models (ALMs) for geographic inference.
Evaluate representative ALMs on AGL1K to quantify performance gaps and failure modes.
impact: Provides a standardized dataset and benchmark that enables rigorous development and comparison of ALMs for geo-localization, accelerating research on geo-aware audio understanding and practical applications (e.g., safety, forensics, environmental monitoring).
visual_elements: World map colored by number of audio samples per country (choropleth) to show geographic coverage
Bar chart comparing model accuracies and common failure cases across key regions
Pipeline diagram showing dataset curation → model input (audio + text) → geo-prediction → evaluation metrics
Example audio spectrograms with location icons and short captions illustrating distinguishable acoustic cues
paper_title: The Sonar Moment: Benchmarking Audio-Language Models in Audio Geo-Localization
paper_authors: Ruixing Zhang, Zihan Liu, Leilei Sun, Tongyu Zhu, Weifeng Lv
